newsitem.title: UK: Dollar firm, Euro shares consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firm, Euro shares consolidate.

text.p: The dollar added to its recent gains on Tuesday while key European stock markets consolidated after Monday's lively rebound as Wall Street slipped lower.
The U.S. currency touched a 56-month peak above 126 yen and five-week highs just short of 1.72 marks, although it had eased back somewhat by mid-afternoon.

"There is no real indication that dollar/yen is suffering from fatigue, either in terms of direction or in the extent of its move," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The British pound traded at 4-1/2 year highs above its old floor of 2.7780 marks in the European exchange rate mechanism, from which it baled out in September 1992.
Prospects for higher U.S. interest rates and the start of Japan's new fiscal year, when new investment decisions are made, are helping to boost the dollar against the yen.
Increasing odds in favour of a single euro currency being launched on time have also helped to depress the mark at the expense of the dollar, analysts said.
They were wary of possible official moves to curb the dollar's gains, which total around two percent this month, although official views in Japan seemed mixed.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said Japan would deal appropriately with excessive currency movements and Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said the authorities would be ready to intervene if necessary.
But Japan's Vice Trade Minister Tsutomu Makino was quoted as saying the weak yen was more positive than negative for the country's economy at the moment.
"We have had some jaw-boning from Japanese policy makers already and that is likely to intensify. If it does, dollar/yen is unlikely to rise sharply," said Meggyesi.

"The Bank of Japan seems to be more relaxed about the strength of the dollar and intervention -- verbal or otherwise -- is not likely until the 128/29-yen level," said a senior trader at a Belgian bank.
Whatever the perceptions in Tokyo, another trader added: "The next focus is what the U.S. auto-manufacturers will say as they feel the pinch of the strong dollar."
On Wall Street the Dow Jones industrial average was down around 20 points or a third of a percent after 45 minutes, shedding most of its net gains from Monday.
The London stock market, Europe's biggest, was around a quarter of a percent lower in mid-afternoon, with investors fretting about the New York market's volatility and higher interest rates to come.

Dealers said the potential for more share price gains in London was limited as concern over interest rates, the strength of the pound and the British election on May 1 had sent buyers to the sidelines.
"There's no business around," one senior dealer complained. "Institutions in the UK don't want to get involved until after the election."
Frankfurt's DAX index ended bourse floor trade up half a percent but was below levels seen in after-hours trading on Monday. It slipped further in post-bourse computerised business.

Traders said German shares paused for breath after Monday's three percent surge and they were waiting for the market to consolidate before pushing prices higher. There was no impetus for further progress despite the dollar's climb above 1.71 marks, good news for exporters.
In Paris the bourse had lost earlier profits to be just marginally higher, slipping back after early progress on the back of the dollar's strength and Wall Street's gains on Monday.
Markets generally were looking ahead to Friday, when U.S. producer prices and retail sales data will give further clues on the timing of the next expected rise in the U.S. interest rates.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7135 marks and 126.33 yen, up from 1.7082 and 125.73 in late European trade on Monday and compared with highs of 1.7183 and 126.52.
The pound traded around 2.7830 marks, above the previous close of 2.7815 but below a high of 2.7915.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 10.9 points or 0.26 percent at 4,260.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade up 16.88 points or 0.51 percent at 3,329.76. But the IBIS DAX for electronic trade was down 26.30 points or 0.79 percent at 3,316.47.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was up 1.10 points or 0.04 percent at 2,573.41.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1415 GMT
Gold traded around $348.55 an ounce after being fixed in the afternoon at $349.10, compared with the previous London close of $349.30. Silver added one cent to $4.81.
